## Why Statistical Programming in R?

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Why R?

* **Public Health Standard:** CDC, WHO, FDA, academic journals, and health agencies run on R.
* **Tidyverse Ecosystem:** Unmatched tools for data wrangling (`dplyr`), visualization (`ggplot2`), and modeling.
* **Open & Reproducible:** Free, community-driven, transparent science.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Why *This* Course?

* No prior programming required.
* **Full data pipeline:** Import $\rightarrow$ Clean $\rightarrow$ Visualize $\rightarrow$ Simulate $\rightarrow$ Report.
* **Modern professional toolkit:** Quarto + Git/GitHub + Responsible AI assistance.
:::
:::

## The Modern Data Science Stack

In this course, you will master five core technologies:

1. **R:** The statistical computing engine.
2. **RStudio / Positron:** The integrated development environment (IDE).
3. **Quarto (`.qmd`):** Reproducible scientific publishing (replaces Word/PDF/slides).
4. **Git & GitHub:** Version control, collaboration, and automated grading.
5. **AI Assistants:** Prompting, verifying, and debugging code with LLMs.

## Choosing Your IDE: RStudio vs. Positron

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### 🟦 RStudio Desktop (Class Standard)

* **Primary demo environment** used on screen during class.
* Matches 1-to-1 with screenshots in **_R Programming: Zero to Pro_** (Ch 1).
* Classic 4-pane layout (Source, Console, Environment, Plots).
* Pre-installed on NYU Bobst library workstations.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### 🟣 Positron (Supported Alternative)

* Posit's next-generation IDE built on **VS Code**.
* Superb native **GitHub Copilot & AI sidecar** integration *(we will demo this in Week 8!)*.
* Native R + Python multi-language switching.
* **100% compatible:** All course Quarto files and Git repos run identically in both!
:::
:::

# Cycle 1: R Fundamentals & Packages {background-color="#2c3e50"}

## R as an Interactive Calculator

You type commands into the **Console**; R evaluates them and prints results.

```r
# Arithmetic
12 + 35
(100 - 32) * 5 / 9   # Fahrenheit to Celsius

# Math functions
sqrt(64)
exp(1)
log(10)              # Natural logarithm (base e)
log10(100)           # Common logarithm (base 10)
```

::: {.callout-tip}
Everything after `#` is a comment and is ignored by R. Use comments to document your thinking!
:::

## Objects and Variable Assignment

We store values in named objects using the assignment operator `<-` (`Alt + -` or `Option + -`):

```r
# Assigning a value
participant_age <- 28
height_m <- 1.75
weight_kg <- 68.5

# Using objects in expressions
bmi <- weight_kg / (height_m^2)
bmi
```

* Names must start with a letter and can contain letters, numbers, `_`, and `.`.
* R is **case-sensitive** (`bmi` $\neq$ `BMI`).

## Functions and Getting Help

Functions take **arguments** (inputs) and return an **output**:

```r
# Rounding
round(bmi, digits = 1)

# Summary statistics
vals <- c(10, 20, 30, NA)
mean(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
```

### Getting help in R:

* `?round` or `help(round)` — opens the official documentation.
* `example(round)` — runs examples from the help page.

## Packages & The Course Textbook: R02Pro

R packages extend R with datasets and specialized functions.

```r
# Install once per computer (done in Console, not script):
install.packages("r02pro")

# Load in every session where you need it:
library(r02pro)
```

* **Textbook:** *R Programming: Zero to Pro* (Free online: [r02pro.github.io](https://r02pro.github.io/)).

# Cycle 2: Reproducible Reports with Quarto {background-color="#2c3e50"}

## Why Quarto?

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### ❌ The Traditional Way

1. Run code in R $\rightarrow$ Copy table to Excel $\rightarrow$ Paste into Word $\rightarrow$ Export PDF.
2. **Data changes?** Repeat everything manually and risk copy-paste errors!
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### ✅ The Quarto Way

One reproducible `.qmd` document combining:

* **Narrative text** (Markdown)
* **Executable code** (R chunks)
* **Dynamic tables & plots** compiled directly on demand.
:::
:::

## Anatomy of a Quarto Document (`.qmd`)

A `.qmd` document combines three elements:

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**1. YAML Metadata (Header):**
```yaml
---
title: "My Analysis"
author: "Your Name"
format: html
---
```

**2. Markdown Narrative (Text):**
```markdown
## Introduction
Here is text with **bold** & *italics*.
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**3. Code Chunks (Live Computation):**
```r
# An R code chunk
mean_age <- mean(c(25, 30, 45))
mean_age
```

**$\longrightarrow$ Click Render (`Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + K`)** to compile directly into a polished HTML report!
:::
:::


## Markdown Text Formatting Cheat Sheet

| Syntax | Rendered Output |
| :--- | :--- |
| `# Heading 1` | **Largest Section Header** |
| `## Heading 2` | **Sub-section Header** |
| `**bold text**` | **bold text** |
| `*italic text*` | *italic text* |
| `- item 1` | Bulleted list |
| `1. item 1` | Numbered list |
| `$E = mc^2$` | Inline math: $E = mc^2$ |

## Code Chunk Options

Control how code executes and displays using `#|`:

```r
#| echo: true       # Show code in final report (default)
#| eval: true       # Run code (default)
#| warning: false   # Suppress package warnings
#| message: false   # Suppress package startup messages
#| fig-width: 7     # Control plot width
```

Click the **Render** button (or `Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + K`) in RStudio to generate your HTML report!

# Cycle 3: Git, GitHub, and Classroom {background-color="#2c3e50"}

## Why Version Control?

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
### ❌ The File Chaos (Without Git)

* `report_v1.docx`
* `report_v2.docx`
* `report_v2_edit.docx`
* `report_final_REALLY_FINAL.docx`
* 😱 *Which file has the correct numbers?*
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
### ✅ The Git Way

* **Recorded history:** Every change is a snapshot with a commit message.
* **Safe experiments:** Try new ideas on branches without breaking main code.
* **Seamless team collaboration:** No emailed zip files or overwritten work.
:::
:::


## The Core Git Workflow in RStudio


## How Homework Works (Instant Feedback)

1. **Accept:** Click the **accept link** for `weekly-exercise-01` on the Week 1 page (after joining the org and linking your NetID).
2. **Clone:** In RStudio $\rightarrow$ *New Project $\rightarrow$ Version Control $\rightarrow$ Git $\rightarrow$ Paste URL*.
3. **Solve:** Open `exercise.qmd`, assign answers to `q1`, `q2`, etc.
4. **Render:** Confirm the HTML compiles cleanly.
5. **Push:** Commit and push to GitHub.
6. **Instant Report:** Go to the **Actions** tab on GitHub: within 2 minutes, see which questions pass.
7. **Iterate:** Revise and re-push freely until Wednesday 11:59 PM!


# Cycle 4: AI Policy & Next Steps {background-color="#57068c"}

## The Three AI Zones

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="33%"}
### 🟢 Zone 1: HW & Project

* **AI Encouraged**
* Use verify-then-use.
* Disclose prompts & changes in AI appendix.
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
### 🔴 Zone 2: Quizzes

* **Strictly No AI**
* 5 bi-weekly 15-min hand-fluency checks.
* Paper or locked browser.
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
### 🟡 Zone 3: In-Class

* **AI Allowed**
* Discuss with pair first.
* Ask CA / Instructor if stuck.
:::
:::

## AI Corner: The "Verify-Then-Use" Rule

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### ❌ The Bad AI User

* Prompts: *"Do my homework question 3."*
* Copies and pastes code blindly.
* Submits hallucinated functions or incorrect math without understanding.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### ✅ The Statistical Programmer

* Prompts: *"How do I compute the trimmed mean in R while handling NAs?"*
* Inspects the output against R documentation.
* Tests edge cases.
* Owns and understands every line.
:::
:::
